SpecGuard.title: Scan: a configuration failure in any part fails the job, keeping the parts that succeeded
SpecGuard.body:
Fixes U6 (unknown-unknown review, 2026-10-17, section 2).

**Problem.** #222 makes a configuration failure (auth, quota, model, policy) fail the job, but only when the whole engine run failed. In a split scan, if part 1 succeeds and part 2 gets 402, the adapter ends the run as success. The reason stays as text in scan-parts, `engine-error` is absent, audit-post says `incomplete`, and the gate exits 0 even with fail_on_error=true. An account that runs dry mid-scan stays green.

**Fix.**
- `src/engines/claude-api.js`: the split-scan loop remembers the first part that failed with a configuration class and writes `engine-error` (same file and format as the single call: `class\nreason`; the reason ends with "N of M parts were reviewed"). The run still ends as success, so the successful parts' findings and the incomplete status are kept.
- `src/fail-on-error.js`: a configuration class in `engine-error` fails the job when STATUS is `incomplete` too, not only `failed`. Message: `SpecGuard could not finish the scan (quota): ...; 1 of 3 parts were reviewed; the partial result was kept`.

**Invariant.** Any configuration failure of the engine, in any call, turns the job red; partial results are still published.

**Unchanged.** Transient part failures (rate, 5xx, network, timeout), the budget stop, and fast-tier reduced reviews: incomplete, warning only. Incomplete with no `engine-error`: exit 0.

**PR mode.** Not affected: only `CHECK=audit` splits into parts; a PR review is one call (one retry for rate or schema inside it), so a configuration failure there already ends the run as failed.

**Tests** (`src/claude-api.test.js`, real planner + adapter + audit-post + fail-on-error, synthetic fetch):
- `scan parts: 200 then quota ...` and `... then auth ...` (fail on main)
- `scan parts: 200 then a rate limit ...`, `scan parts: the budget stop ...` (controls)
- `fail-on-error.js: incomplete without engine-error, with a non-configuration class, or reduced exits 0; ...` (fails on main; covers the no-engine-error and reduced controls)
- `src/audit-action.test.js`: the existing "incomplete is not a failure" loop no longer lists `incomplete` with class auth; that case now expects exit 1, since that is the changed behaviour.

Touched test files pass (184 tests, 0 fail, 1 skip). Full suite: CI.

**User-visible change.** A split scan that loses a part to auth/quota/model/policy now fails the job (red) while still posting the findings of the parts that succeeded.

SpecGuard.title: Weekly report: the API git stand-in keeps unknown, renames and -w like real git (U1–U3); pin the coverage-row FP contract (U4)
SpecGuard.body:
Fixes U1-U3 from the 2026-10-17 unknown-unknown review in the weekly report's API git stand-in (`apiGit`/`unified0`), and pins the U4 grading contract. No second outcome rule: post.js's own `anchorTouched`/`testsChanged` still decide.

**U1 (unknown stays unknown).** A modified file with no `patch` (large or binary diff) now throws from the stand-in, so post.js returns null. A target file missing from a commit's file list of 300 or more (GitHub's cap) throws too. The name-only branch does the same when the list may be cut and no test path was seen.

**U2 (renames).** The name-only branch returns `previous_filename` and `filename` for renamed entries, like `--no-renames`. `app.test.js` renamed to `app.js`, and the reverse, now give tests_changed = true.

**U3 (`-w`).** With `-w`, `unified0` drops a change run whose removed and added lines are equal after removing all whitespace, pairwise and with equal line counts. Ceiling (commented as `ponytail:`): git's `-w` can realign hunks, so this is an approximation.

**U4 (contract, no code change).** A coverage row counts as a request for action only when its gap's finding is actionable. A row whose finding is low-confidence or in Details is not an FP. A row with no finding still is (S10). Written at `rowFps` in `eval/grade.js`.

Tests:
- `eval/weekly-report.test.js`: `apiGit U1`, `apiGit U2`, `apiGit U3`. U3 compares against real git in a temp repo (GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1, temp HOME). Controls: patch present gives true, a complete file list gives false, a direct edit to a test file gives true, a non-whitespace replace gives true.
- `eval/grade.test.js`: `coverage-row FP contract` (real buildSummary, real grade). It passes on main, as intended.
- U1, U2 and U3 fail on main. Evidence: U1 `actual: false, expected: null`; U2 `actual: false, expected: true`; U3 `ws: actual: true, expected: false`.

Not fixed: `-w` hunk realignment (see U3 ceiling). Files beyond 300 per commit are treated as unknown, not paginated.
Full suite: CI.

SpecGuard.title: Keep secret-like files' diffs out of the model input
SpecGuard.body:
## Problem
Secret-like files changed in a PR reached the model through the diff. `collect.sh` wrote `git diff` for every listed file, and `IGNORES` has no `.env`, `*.pem` or `id_rsa`. The `DENY` list in `claude-api.js` only guarded file reads (`packRead`, `nothingToRead`), not the diff path. A probe with `.env`, `config/.env.production`, `secrets.pem`, `id_rsa` and `app.js` (synthetic literal only) put all four secret hunks into the assembled prompt and the claude-api user message. The CLI engines read the same prompt file.

## Fix
- `claude-api.js` exports `DENY` (one definition, no second list).
- New `src/deny-filter.js`: reads paths on stdin, prints the `DENY` matches.
- `collect.sh`: after the file, spec and dropped-doc lists are built and before any diff, numbered diff, focus or spec text is made, deny-matching paths are removed and written to `denied.txt`. Every engine gets the same filtered input.
- Fail closed: if the filter cannot run, collect writes `collect-error.txt`, sets `skip=true` and sends no diff. `post.js` already publishes that as a failed run.
- Deny-only PR: the file list ends empty, so the existing "nothing reviewable" skip fires. The model is not called. The summary says why: "Nothing to review: every changed file is ignored (...) or secret-like. Not reviewed: N secret-like file(s) (...): their diff was not sent to the model."
- `post.js`: otherwise one `Not reviewed: N secret-like file(s) (\`.env\`, \`secrets.pem\`): their diff was not sent to the model` line goes through the existing not-reviewed channel (`addNote`).

## Complete or incomplete?
Complete. The files are excluded on purpose, like ignored files. Marking the run incomplete would make a re-run permanent and useless, since the same files would be excluded again. The note keeps the scope honest without a perpetual "incomplete" state.

## Scan / audit path
Already covered. Repository files for the scan are packed only through `contextPack` / `windowPack` / `evidencePack`, and all of them read through `packRead`, which applies `DENY`. `audit-collect.js` only lists tracked paths and does not send file text. No change needed.

## `.env.example`
`DENY` matches `.env.example` (and any `.env.*`). Kept denied: one definition, and templates are sometimes committed with real values. The cost is that the file is listed under Not reviewed. Changing the shared `DENY` would also change file reads, which is out of scope here.

## Tests
- `collect.test.js`
  - "secret-like files changed in a PR never reach diff.patch, the numbered diff or the prompt; ..." (probe scenario, four files, literal absent from `diff.patch`, `diff.numbered.txt` and the assembled prompt; the `app.js` hunk is kept)
  - "a PR that changes only secret-like files is an honest skip ..."
  - "fail closed: when the secret-path filter cannot run ..."
  - "control: look-alike names (env.js, src/environment.ts, keys.test.js) are not dropped"
- `post.test.js`
  - "denied.txt: secret-like files show one Not reviewed line ... and do not make the run incomplete"
  - "denied.txt: a PR with only secret-like files is a complete skip that names them"
- The existing "a failing requirements step records unavailable" test used a `NODE_OPTIONS` crash, which now (correctly) trips the fail-closed filter. It now uses a `requirements.js` stub that exits 1. Same assertions. The stub-scenario helper runs the real `deny-filter.js` so a stubbed `trace.js` does not break it.
- On main (origin/main `collect.sh` / `post.js` swapped in): the first three collect tests and both post tests fail (for example `diff.patch carries a secret-file line`, and `skip=true` missing from the output). The control only asserted an absent `denied.txt` and passes on main once written as `!denied.txt`.
- Local: `collect.test.js` + `post.test.js` 313 pass, 0 fail. Full suite: CI.

## Not fixed, follow-ups
- `copilot.sh --allow-all-tools` and `claude.sh` agent-mode file tools can still read a `.env` from the checkout. The model can open it by path. Out of scope here.
- Secrets inside non-secret-named files are not detected (name-based only).

SpecGuard.title: Fail the job when the model cannot run because of configuration (bad key, no credit, unknown model)
SpecGuard.body:
## Incident

From 2026-10-15 21:05 to 10-16 12:28 every SpecGuard dogfood run (63 runs, 19 PRs between #197 and #218) failed with "The Anthropic API key was rejected (check the llm_token secret)". Every job stayed green, so PRs were merged on green checks. The only signal was an in-place PR comment ("Could not complete: ..."). The log never held the HTTP status.

Cause: a 401 wrote `engine-status=failed` and a `::warning::`, the step exited 0, and `fail-on-error.js` ran only when `fail_on_error == 'true'` (default false, and nothing on PR or schedule events sets it).

## Change

- A configuration failure always fails the job, whatever `fail_on_error` is: class `auth` (missing key, 401, 403), `quota` (402 or "credit balance"), `model` (unknown or not allowed). Message: `::error::SpecGuard could not run the model (<class>): <reason>`. The PR comment keeps its "Could not complete" line.
- Transient failures (rate 429/529, 5xx, network, timeout) and the user's own budget stay advisory unless `fail_on_error: true`. The warning now names the class: `::warning::SpecGuard could not complete (rate): ...`.
- `action.yml`: the last step runs on every non-cancelled run and receives `FAIL_ON_ERROR`. `fail-on-error.js` reads the class from the first line of `engine-error`, the channel the engines already write. No new file. It covers PR and scan mode (both post steps feed the same STATUS/REASON, and both read `engine-error`).
- `claude-api.js`: the engine log is now `Claude review failed (auth, HTTP 401): <reason>`. Never the key or the response body. Auth reasons are split: no key "No API key was provided (set llm_token)", 401 "rejected", 403 "lacks permission for this model or workspace". 429/529 were already `rate`, separate from credit/billing `quota`.
- `copilot.sh`: its `quota` class matched both an account quota and the AI-credit cap. The credit cap is now class `budget` (advisory, same text). Its `auth` goes red under the same rule.
- Docs: `fail_on_error` in action.yml, specguard.yml and README; engines README.

## Tests (all but the classify control fail on main)

- `fail-on-error.js: a configuration failure (auth, quota, model) fails the job without fail_on_error; ...`: auth/quota/model with FAIL_ON_ERROR unset exit 1 with the `::error::` line. Controls: rate/budget/timeout/unclassified exit 0 (warning names the class), exit 1 with `FAIL_ON_ERROR=true`, complete/incomplete/skip/empty exit 0.
- `auth reasons tell the owner what to fix ...` (no key / 401 / 403 text, log has class and HTTP status).
- `classify: credit/billing is quota ...; 429 and 529 are rate` (control, passes on main too).
- Changed: the structure test "runs fail-on-error.js only when fail_on_error is true" now asserts `!cancelled()` plus `FAIL_ON_ERROR` passed through, because the step must run on every run to see configuration failures. Existing `fail-on-error.js` tests now set `FAIL_ON_ERROR=true` where they assert the old red-on-any-failure behaviour. Log-line regexes in two claude-api tests gained the class tag. The copilot AI-credits case expects `budget`.

## Not covered

- `claude.sh` agent mode has no HTTP status (CLI text only), so its log has no status and its auth text is not split. It does write the same `auth`/`quota`/`model` classes, so the new rule applies.
- Copilot `policy` (org disabled) is a config issue too but outside the three classes asked for; left advisory.
- The `dogfood` check will itself go red if the repo's key is still bad. That is the intended behaviour.

Behaviour change users will notice: a PR check turns red when the key, credit or model is wrong, even with `fail_on_error` unset.

SpecGuard.title: Count reduced-review degradations by an explicit id, not note wording
SpecGuard.body:
Follows up review comments on #215 and #217.

## What
- `reducedReasons` used to count degraded obligations by regex-matching validation note text (`Obligation X marked unknown: ...`). Now `degrade(data, id, text)` pushes the note and records the id in `data.degraded`, and `reducedReasons` counts `data.degraded` only. Rewording a note can no longer change whether a run is reduced.
- `validate()` always overwrites `degraded` with its own list, so a model-supplied `degraded` is never trusted.
- Adds an end-to-end PR-mode test with the real cover guard (#217 follow-up), and a comment documenting why the unscoped search is safe (files absent from `test-candidates.txt` are in `candidates-cut.txt`, which already makes the run incomplete).

## Every "marked unknown" site
| Site | Counted? | Why |
|---|---|---|
| post.js validate(): malformed coverage row (`marked unknown: ${why}`) | yes, `degraded.push` | the old regex counted it; row failed on its own content |
| post.js validate(): `needs exactly one <status> finding` demotion | yes, `degraded.push` | old regex counted it |
| verifyEvidence: citation could not be verified | yes, `degrade()` | old regex counted it |
| verifyEvidence: cited evidence is not a running assertion | yes, `degrade()` | old regex counted it |
| applyCoverage: coverage report shows the line never ran | yes, `degrade()` | old regex counted it |
| verifyRequirements: `marked unknown: The linked requirement ...` | no | old regex excluded it (row only unverified via a requirement link); plain note |
| verifyRequirements: `alignment unknown: requirement wording not verified` | no | alignment only, status unchanged |
| settle(): `alignment unknown: ...` | no | derived alignment, not a degraded row |
| verifyEvidence E1 `not covered: only truthiness/interaction assertions` (#215) | no | deliberately does not trip reduced mode; says "not covered", never matched |
| audit-post.js:140 `${w} marked unknown` | no | different pipeline (audit), not `Obligation`, never reached reducedReasons |

## Other readers of validation_notes text
No other decision reads note wording. `gapFree` (post.js:510) checks only whether any note exists; the summary (post.js:879) renders them. Not touched.

## Tests
- `reduced: each of the four triggers...`: new "wording only" assertion (note text without the id does not count). Helper builds `degraded` the way validation does.
- `degrades only the part with a semantic problem...`: asserts `degraded` ids for a malformed row and a demotion, and that a forged model `degraded` is overwritten.
- `the real cover guard in PR mode...`: unrelated test with the same literal does not demote (control); the cited file's candidate test does.

## Fail on main
With main's `src/post.js` swapped in (restored after):
- reduced triggers: FAIL, `note text that says "marked unknown" is not a degradation without the explicit kind`
- degrades only the part...: FAIL, `a malformed row is recorded by id`
- real cover guard test: PASSES on main. It is a regression pin for #217's behaviour, not a bug repro.

`node --test src/post.test.js`: 271 pass, 0 fail. Full suite is the CI gate.

## Behaviour change
None intended. Same rows count as before; only the mechanism changed.

SpecGuard.title: Scan: never adopt another target's scan issue; compare repo names case-insensitively
SpecGuard.body:
Fixes two scan-issue addressing bugs.

**Fixes**
- `findIssue` with no title (same-repo scan) now skips an issue titled for another target (`SpecGuard: unit test gap scan: owner/repo`, optionally followed by a scope). A repo that holds a scan of itself and of a foreign target no longer adopts the foreign one's rotation state and progress. A legacy title with no target, a scoped title, and a title naming this very repo stay ours. An explicit title still selects exactly that issue (now compared case-insensitively).
- `resolveIssueTarget` compares `ISSUE_REPO` with the scanned repo case-insensitively, so `mira190/specguard` vs `Mira190/SpecGuard` is `away=false`.

**Case comparisons audited.** Owner/repo comparisons in the scan path: `resolveIssueTarget` (fixed) and `findIssue` (fixed). `src/requirements.js` already lowercases. `audit-collect.js` loadPrior calls `resolveIssueTarget` and `findIssue`, so it inherits both fixes.

**Collector (c): not ported.** #200 already routes the collector through `resolveIssueTarget`: `src/audit-collect.js:311` takes the target and scope, `:312` uses `ISSUE_TOKEN` when away and `GH_TOKEN` otherwise, `:328` passes the title only when away. No failing test shows a wrong repo or token on main, so nothing was added there. `stateAddress()` was not ported for the same reason.

**Tests** (`src/audit-post.test.js`, fake client):
- scan issue: with a foreign target issue listed first, the own issue is picked
- scan issue: a foreign target issue alone is never adopted
- scan issue: an explicit title still selects that issue, case-insensitively
- scan issue control: a single own issue (plain, scoped, or titled for this very repository) is found
- scan issue: ISSUE_REPO differing only in case is the scanned repository (away=false)
- scan issue control: a real foreign ISSUE_REPO is away

On main, 4 fail and the 2 controls pass. The explicit-title test fails on main only at its upper-case assertion.

**Not fixed.** An existing foreign issue that was adopted in the past is not migrated; the next run simply finds the own issue or creates one.

**User-visible change.** A repo that scans itself and a foreign target stops mixing their state. A first run after this may create a fresh own issue where it used to reuse the foreign one.

SpecGuard.title: Eval: count wrong coverage rows as FPs; weekly anchor/tests rule matches post.js (S9, S10)
SpecGuard.body:
Fixes S9 and S10 from the supplement audit.

**S10 (eval/grade.js).** A coverage row saying weak_test or missing_test, with no matching summary item and no posted comment, now counts as one false positive and breaks `expect_clean`. It is counted once per F29 group, and not again when a posted comment (same kind/path, within 2 lines) or a summary item already stands for the gap.

**S9 (eval/weekly-report.js).** `anchor_touched` and `tests_changed` now call `post.anchorTouched` / `post.testsChanged` with an API-backed stand-in for git (`apiGit`, `unified0`). So they follow post.js: first-parent non-merge commits only, a deleted file gives unknown (null), and an unusable compare or unavailable commit gives null, never false. Report output format is unchanged.

Tests added:
- grade.test.js: `S10: a wrong coverage row counts as a false positive...` (fails on main: 0 !== 1); `S10: a coverage row for a gap that is also a posted comment counts once` (benign control, also passes on main; guards the double count found during review).
- weekly-report.test.js: `load: a merged base and a deleted anchor file give the same anchor/tests answer as post.js` (fails on main: true,true vs false,false); `unified0: matches git diff -U0 ...` (add, delete, modify, two runs in one hunk, no-newline, compared with real git in a temp repo; plus null-not-false assertions for a throwing git).

Not in scope: U7, U8, U10, U11 and V2.

SpecGuard.title: Scan funnel: split 'not reached' into the inventory cap and the time budget
SpecGuard.body:
The Units line counted files past the inventory cap and files the time budget never read as one number. The second depends on runner speed, so the line and the scan issue body changed between two runs on the same commit.

The totals now carry not_reached_cap (deterministic for a commit) and not_reached_time (time budget). not_reached stays as their sum. The line shows 'J past the inventory cap' and 'T unread when the time budget ran out', leaving out zero terms. E = I + N + J + T still holds.

inventory() takes an optional maxRead (default is the existing cap) so a test can lower it. Tests cover a lowered cap (J > 0, T = 0), budgetMs: 0 (T > 0), and the rendered line's equation.

SpecGuard.title: Track first-level imports in unit freshness; scope the cover guard to candidate tests
SpecGuard.body:
Fixes E3 and E5 (research F33, Q4).

**E3: a covered unit is never stale when a helper or an imported file changes.**
`ver` in `src/audit-units.js` now also folds in the blob hashes of first-level relative imports: the unit's own, and those of its matched test files (helpers, fixtures). Imports are extracted from blobs already read (no new git calls) and resolved against the tracked tree with the usual extensions and `index` files (`./x.js` also tries `x.ts`). Bare package imports are ignored. One level only (`ponytail:` comment names the ceiling).
Invariant: `ver` changes whenever anything a review of the unit directly saw changes.
Migration: `verLegacy` (ver without imports) is exposed, and a stored legacy ver counts as unchanged, so existing state sees no one-time burst of stale units. A unit with no imports keeps its old ver. `ponytail:` note says to drop `verLegacy` after one rotation.

**E5: an unrelated test demotes a missing_test.**
`makeCoverGuard` takes an optional 4th argument, the eligible test files. A hit counts only inside that set (literal and class+method searches; a delegated helper's test lives with the helper, so that search is not limited). PR mode passes the cited file's candidates from `test-candidates.txt`; scan mode passes the unit's matched tests. Without a set, behaviour is unchanged. An empty set means no demotion: a gap with no candidate tests is more likely real.

Tests added:
- `ver: a weakened test helper or a changed imported file makes the covered unit stale; an unrelated file does not; a legacy ver is not a change` (audit-units.test.js)
- `makeCoverGuard: an eligible-test set limits a hit to the claim's own candidate tests (wave 4 E5)` (test-map.test.js)
- `the cover guard is asked about the cited file's candidate tests only (wave 4 E5)...` (post.test.js)

Fail on origin/main (source files swapped in): helper test fails at "a weakened helper of a matched test makes the unit stale"; guard test fails on the unrelated-test case; post test gets `['src.js', undefined]` instead of the candidate list.

Test changed: `TEST_PATHS reaches the scan post step` now lists qa/checks/orders.js as the unit's matched test (before, a unit with no matched tests was demoted by any test; that is the E5 behaviour being removed).

Not fixed: imports deeper than one level, Python/Go imports.
User-visible: units whose imports changed are re-reviewed (marked "changed since, due again"); a missing_test is no longer lowered by a test outside the file's candidates.
Full suite: not run locally; CI is the gate. audit-post, audit-units, test-map tests pass locally (115).

SpecGuard.title: Scan report: reconcile the unit funnel in one visible line
SpecGuard.body:
Fixes E6 (scan funnel).

- inventory totals gain `eligible` = inventoried + not inventoried (over 512 KiB), so E = I + N holds by construction.
- The visible code-first section gets one line: Units: E eligible = I inventoried + N not inventoried (over 512 KiB); S selected this run = R reviewed whole + C did not fit + F forced (recorded unsure); D not yet reviewed. Zero terms are omitted.
- Details no longer says "The K riskiest of M units were reviewed"; it says "R of the S selected units were reviewed whole".
- Details row of a unit that did not fit: "selected, did not fit (not reviewed)"; forced: "forced: tests cut (unsure)" (was "this run").

Invariant: the counts shown add up, and no statement says a unit was reviewed when it was not.

Tests: render: the funnel line reconciles eligible, selected, reviewed, did not fit and forced (in src/audit-code.test.js; includes the all-reviewed control); the existing 512 KiB inventory test asserts eligible = units + not_inventoried (src/audit-units.test.js). The old Details wording assertion was updated to the new text.

Not changed: audit-units ver, test-map, evidence verification (other agents). Behaviour change: new Units line in the visible report; D counts did-not-fit units as not yet reviewed.

SpecGuard.title: Evidence tiers: weak-only assertions do not cover; refuted counterexamples demoted (E1, E2)
SpecGuard.body:
Fixes wave-4 E1 and E2.

**E1** A value obligation stayed `covered` when its only cited evidence was a truthiness or interaction-only assertion. New shared classifier `post.weakAssertion` (next to `ASSERTION`): `ok`, `toBeTruthy/Falsy/Defined`, `not.toBeNull/Undefined`, bare `toHaveBeenCalled()`, `toHaveBeenCalledTimes`, `toThrow()` with no argument are weak. Everything else, including unknown syntax, is value (fail open). In `verifyEvidence` (PR) and `audit-post.verify` (scan), a covered row whose verified assertions are all weak becomes `unknown` with a reason. No finding is posted; findings on the row are dropped by the existing unknown-row filter.
Invariant: "covered" needs at least one cited assertion that pins an expected value.

**E2** A weak_test counterexample refuted by the cited assertion was accepted at high confidence. New `post.refutedBy(quote, counterexample)`: exact equality against a primitive literal (`assert.equal/strictEqual/deepEqual/deepStrictEqual`, `expect().toBe/toEqual/toStrictEqual`), and the counterexample says the same EXPR (whitespace-normalised) returns a different literal. Then `validate` demotes to low with `gated = true` and adds a validation note; audit-post `verifyUnits` marks the unit finding low. Different input, several claims or unparsed syntax: unchanged.
Invariant: a counterexample cannot contradict the assertion it cites.

Tests: `E1 PR`, `E2` (post.test.js); `E1 scan`, `E2 scan` (audit-post.test.js). Each fails on origin/main (4 of 4). Controls: `assert.equal(discount(100), 90)`, `toHaveBeenCalledWith(100)`, one weak + one value assertion still cover; `assert.ok(f(1))` + "f(1) returns 'oops'" and a different-input counterexample stay high.

Touched test files: 348 tests, 347 pass, 0 fail, 1 skipped. Full suite left to CI.

Not fixed: helper-wrapped assertions and `assert(x)` / `assert.throws(fn)` without matcher are treated as value (fail open). Behaviour change: rows backed only by weak assertions now show as unknown instead of covered.

SpecGuard.title: Fix rerun skip key, --fail-on-gaps exit code, reusable workflow inputs, example boundary (S13, U4, S12, U9)
SpecGuard.body:
Fixes supplement findings S13, U4, S12, U9.

## S13: rerun skip key ignored config, model and version
- post.js writes `<!-- specguard:cfg=<sha8> -->` into the sticky summary. `cfgKey` (src/preflight.js, one function used by both post.js and preflight) hashes the SpecGuard build (src/version.js) plus one `CFG` string that action.yml builds from the same inputs for both steps: engine, model, effort, auto_tier, fast_models, max_comments, max_diff_kb, focus_threshold, focus_files, ignore, standards_checks, standards_ref, requirements_paths, test_paths, standards_paths, coverage_files, trace.
- Preflight skips only when the head, req and issues markers match AND the cfg marker equals the current one. A summary with no cfg marker (written before this change) does not skip: one re-review per open PR after upgrade.
- Invariant: a rerun is skipped only if the earlier review used the same code and the same review inputs.
- Not in the hash: the rule files' content. They are read from the base commit by collect.sh, which runs after preflight, so they are not available at preflight time (`ponytail:` comment in src/preflight.js). Editing a rule file alone does not trigger a re-review; `force: true` does. model/engine are the raw inputs (preflight runs before credential resolution), so a change of the resolved model through `auto` is not seen.
- Tests: `a rerun on the same head is skipped only when the config marker matches` (same everything skips, changed model reviews, no cfg marker reviews, no CFG env is not checked), `post.js writes the cfg marker that preflight computes from the same CFG`.

## U4: `--fail-on-gaps` exited 0 on a failed run
- Exit 1 on a gap, 2 when the status is not `complete` (failed, incomplete), else 0. A gap wins over 2. USAGE and README updated.
- Tests: `U4: --fail-on-gaps exits 2 when the run did not complete` (unparseable findings -> failed; invalid evidence -> reduced/incomplete), control `U4 control: a clean COMPLETE run ... exits 0`.
- Behaviour change: the existing test `main: exit code is 0 (advisory)...` had a "clean" fixture whose cited evidence is not an assertion; post.js reports that as an incomplete (reduced) review, so its last assertion now expects 2. The truly clean control is the new test.
- Not fixed: a run with status `complete` that still holds `unknown` obligations (summary says "part of the review could not be assessed") still exits 0; the spec was the status field.

## S12: reusable workflow forwarded 12 of 47 action inputs
- `.github/workflows/specguard.yml` now declares and forwards every input, with the action's own defaults. Booleans (include_bots, resolve_stale, force, fail_on_error, scan_issue) are `boolean`; the rest `string`. `review_timeout_minutes` and `copilot_max_ai_credits` are inputs whose empty default keeps the old mode-based value (12/25, 60/400). `scan_issue_token` is a new optional secret.
- Documented exclusions (comment in the workflow): `github_token` (the workflow passes github.token), `repository`, `pr_number`, `base_sha`, `head_sha` (manual targeting; this workflow reviews the caller's pull_request event).
- Test `S12: the reusable workflow forwards every action input...` (src/audit-action.test.js): parses action.yml inputs, the workflow `with:` and the exclusion comment, asserts forwarded + excluded == action inputs, that no exclusion is forwarded, and that declared defaults equal the action's.
- Existing tests in src/enterprise-workflows.test.js and the `fail_on_error` check in audit-action.test.js were updated for the larger input list, the third secret and the new `fail_on_error` input (default false).
- The action pin is unchanged. The new inputs take effect when the pin is bumped at release (`node bin/pin-reusable.js`); until then the pinned action ignores inputs it does not know (GitHub only warns).

## U9: example marked a one-sided boundary covered
- `skills/test-review/references/example.json` (and the `.github/skills/test-review` copy, identical): O1 now cites `assert.equal(discount(99), 99);` as well, and the reason names both sides.
- Test `U9: every covered example.json row whose behaviour is a >=/<= boundary cites at least 2 assertions` (also checks the .github copy is identical).

## Verification
- Every new test fails on origin/main (S13: `cfgKey is not a function`; S12: no documented exclusions; U9: `O1 cites 1 assertion(s)`; U4: `failed run 0 !== 2`).
- Local: only the touched test files (preflight, audit-action, enterprise-workflows, post, prompt, credential, specguard-local, pin-reusable): 370 tests, 370 pass. The full suite runs in CI on this PR.

Kite.title: Round confirmed region selection to even width and height
Kite.body:
Design 4.1 says that on confirm the region's width and height are rounded to even numbers (H.264 4:2:0). The overlay result was saved as drawn, so an odd selection like 1033×575 showed up in the preview and settings while the crop was silently floored to 1032×574 later. This adds a pure `evenRegion()` helper in `geometry.ts` and applies it in `overlayDone`, so the saved and displayed size is the recorded size. Position is untouched. It floors, matching the existing `evenFloor`/`regionToCrop` behaviour, and adds a unit test.

Also: the SpecGuard workflow now runs from SpecGuard main with the Claude engine.

Kite.title: ci: full history for the SpecGuard scan
Kite.body: The scan ranks units by churn and fix commits and prioritises changed documents; both need the git history (fetch-depth: 0).

Kite.title: ci: SpecGuard scan from main with the Claude engine
Kite.body: The weekly/dispatch scan moves from the old fix branch and Copilot to SpecGuard main with the Claude engine (secret SPEC), mode scan with the scan issue.

Kite.title: Reject out-of-range durations in the schedule and fixed-length fields
Kite.body:
`parseHms` accepted hours up to 99, so `99:00:00` parsed to 356,400 s. The field committed it, and settings normalisation then silently clamped it to MAX_DUR (23:59:59), so the UI showed one value and saved another.

`parseHms` now returns null unless the value is within 1..MAX_DUR, the same range `normalize` enforces for `schedule.dur` and `fixed.sec`. Both callers (the schedule dialog's duration and the fixed-length field) go through `HmsField`, which now treats null as the existing invalid-input state and no longer needs its own `> 0` checks. The error message mentions the 23:59:59 maximum. `docs/design.md` gets one bullet in 4.2 stating the limits.

Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `parseHms('23:59:59')` returns 86399 (MAX_DUR) and `parseHms('00:00:01')` returns 1.
- [ ] `parseHms` returns null for `24:00:00`, `99:00:00`, `100:00:00` and `00:00:00`, and still returns null for malformed text.
- [ ] Typing an out-of-range duration in either duration field shows the invalid-input state and leaves the saved value unchanged.
- [ ] Valid values still commit on blur / Enter.
- [ ] `npm test` and `npx vite build` pass.
- [ ] `docs/design.md` states the 23:59:59 maximum.

Kite.title: Align main window height and default list selection with design.md
Kite.body:
Brings the code in line with two lines of docs/design.md (spec unchanged):

- "Main window: Regular window, 1000×740, minimum 820×600" - `electron/app.cjs` created it with `height: 800`; now 740.
- "The first row of the recording list carries a 'New' badge and is selected by default, but does not enter editing automatically" - `ListPage` started with an empty selection. The newest row is now selected when the list loads, and when the selected row disappears (or the save folder changes). A row the user picked is kept. Editing is never entered automatically.

The selection rule is a pure function, `defaultSelection` in `src/engine/listselect.ts`, with unit tests in `test/listselect.test.ts`.

Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The main window opens at 1000×740 with a minimum of 820×600.
- [ ] Opening the Recordings page selects the newest row; the rename field is not shown.
- [ ] Picking another row keeps that row selected when the list refreshes.
- [ ] If the selected row is deleted or moved away, the newest remaining row becomes selected.
- [ ] An empty list selects nothing.
- [ ] `npm test` passes (143 tests) and `npx vite build` succeeds.

Kite.title: Scheduled recording can repeat on chosen weekdays
Kite.body:
Scheduled recording was one-shot: it fired once and the switch turned itself off. The plan can now repeat on chosen weekdays (design.md section 4.5).

Changes
- `Schedule.days: number[]` (0-6, Sunday = 0). Empty = the old one-shot behaviour.
- `nextTrigger(now, h, m, s, days)`: next selected weekday at h:m:s, today if still ahead.
- `scheduleText` appends the repeat days, e.g. "00:30:15 后自动开始录制，每周一、三、五重复" / "每天重复".
- Settings: missing `days` (old files) -> `[]`; non-integer / out-of-range values dropped; duplicates merged, sorted.
- `electron/app.cjs`: a repeating plan stays on after it fires and re-arms from the due time (no double fire on an early timer tick); one-shot still switches off.
- Schedule dialog: weekday toggle buttons (Mon-Sun) and updated hint text.
- docs/design.md 4.5 describes scheduled recording and the repeat rule; README line updated.

Acceptance criteria
1. With no weekday selected, `nextTrigger` / `scheduleText` / the plan behave exactly as before (today or tomorrow, switch turns off after firing).
2. With weekdays selected, `nextTrigger` returns the next selected weekday at h:m:s: today if the time is still ahead, otherwise the nearest later selected day (up to 7 days; month and year roll over).
3. A repeating plan stays on after it fires and is armed for the next occurrence.
4. The status text names the repeat days (Monday first; all seven = "每天重复"); off still shows "无计划录制".
5. Old saved settings without `days` load with an empty selection; invalid day values are dropped.
6. The schedule dialog has a weekday picker whose selection is saved immediately.
7. `npm test` passes (142 tests, 0 failures).

Not covered by automated tests: the dialog UI and the re-arm in `electron/app.cjs` (the electron smoke run was not executed).

Review against my #216 note (time-budget churn in the funnel line).

- `not_reached` is split into the deterministic inventory cap (J) and the run-speed-dependent time budget (T). The line still reconciles (E = I + N + J + T), and the test parses it to prove it.
- `not_reached` is kept as J + T in totals, so existing readers see the same number.
- `maxRead` is a test seam with the old constant as default; no behaviour change.

SpecGuard#220.body: P3: `TITLE` is interpolated into a RegExp unescaped. That is safe today because it is a constant with no metacharacters, but a later wording change (e.g. adding `(beta)` or `?`) would silently break the foreign check, and every issue would look "ours" again. SpecGuard#222.body:
**[P2] An account out of Copilot credits must stay red.** `budget limit` / `AI credits exceeded` is the account's or org's premium-request cap, set in GitHub billing. SpecGuard has no per-run Copilot cap, so this is not a deliberate per-run limit the user chose for this run. Like Anthropic `quota`, only the owner can fix it, and every push until then would fail the same way. Classing it as advisory `budget` recreates exactly the incident this PR fixes, for Copilot users: green checks, no review, for days.

Please revert this split, so both branches stay `quota`, and keep the test expecting `quota`. The advisory `budget` class should stay reserved for SpecGuard's own per-run `max_budget_usd` stop (claude-api's preflight), which is the user's deliberate limit.

Review against the 2026-10-15/16 incident (63 dogfood runs and 19 PRs green while the key was rejected).

- The rule is right and it's in the one place every mode passes through: configuration failures always go red, and transient ones stay advisory unless `fail_on_error`. The class comes from the existing `engine-error` channel, and the step now runs on every non-cancelled run, so PR, scan and dispatch are all covered.
- The log line now carries the class and HTTP status without the body, so the next incident is greppable.
- The 401/403/no-key reasons tell the owner what to fix.
- The fail-on-main evidence is real (auth/quota/model exited 0 on main).

One P2 and one P3 inline. The P2 reintroduces the incident class for Copilot users, so please fix it before merge.

-w keeps a run whose line counts differ

No test has removed and added runs of different length, so dropping the 'run.dl.length === run.al.length' clause still passes the suite. Input: removed 'line 7;', added 'line 7;' and 'extra;' gives the run kept (true) by the current code and by git -w. Without the count check, the pairwise compare drops the run and the result is false. Add to weekly-report.test.js:

test('apiGit U3: -w keeps a run whose removed and added line counts differ', () => {
  const { post, a, b, git } = stand();
  const patch = '@@ -7,1 +7,2 @@\n-line 7;\n+line 7;\n+extra;';
  assert.equal(post.anchorTouched(a, b, 'app.js', 7, 7, null, git([{ filename: 'app.js', status: 'modified', patch }])), true);
});

workflows.kite_pr:
name: SpecGuard
on:
  pull_request:
    types: [opened, synchronize, reopened, ready_for_review]
concurrency: { group: "specguard-${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}", cancel-in-progress: true }
permissions:
  contents: read
  pull-requests: write
  issues: read
  copilot-requests: write
jobs:
  review:
    if: ${{ !github.event.pull_request.draft && github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@d23441a48e516b6c34aea4fa41551a30e30af803 # v6.1.0
        with: { fetch-depth: 0, persist-credentials: false }
      - uses: Mira190/SpecGuard@main # pilot: pin a SHA once stable
        with:
          llm_token: ${{ secrets.SPEC }} # Anthropic key (sk-ant-...): the claude engine is picked by the prefix
workflows.kite_scan:
name: SpecGuard audit
on:
  workflow_dispatch:
  schedule:
    - cron: "0 20 * * 0"
permissions:
  contents: read
  issues: write
  copilot-requests: write
jobs:
  audit:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@d23441a48e516b6c34aea4fa41551a30e30af803 # v6.1.0
        with: { fetch-depth: 0, persist-credentials: false }
      - uses: Mira190/SpecGuard@main # pilot: pin a SHA once stable
        with:
          mode: scan
          scan_issue: "true"
          llm_token: ${{ secrets.SPEC }} # Anthropic key: the claude engine
          review_timeout_minutes: "25"
workflows.specguard_ci:
name: CI
on:
  pull_request:
    types: [opened, synchronize, reopened, ready_for_review]
  push: { branches: [main] }
concurrency: { group: "ci-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.ref }}", cancel-in-progress: true }
permissions:
  contents: read
  pull-requests: write
  issues: read
  copilot-requests: write
jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@d23441a48e516b6c34aea4fa41551a30e30af803 # v6.1.0
        with: { persist-credentials: false }
      - uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0
        with: { node-version: 22 }
      - run: node --test src/*.test.js bin/*.test.js eval/*.test.js $(find eval-sandbox -name "*.test.js" 2>/dev/null) # sandbox tests exist only on eval PRs; never run eval/cases fixtures
      - run: diff -r skills/test-review .github/skills/test-review && diff ccr/test-review.instructions.md .github/instructions/test-review.instructions.md
  dogfood:
    if: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' && !github.event.pull_request.draft && github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 20
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@d23441a48e516b6c34aea4fa41551a30e30af803 # v6.1.0
        with: { fetch-depth: 0, persist-credentials: false }
      - uses: ./
        with:
          review_timeout_minutes: "15"
          ignore: eval/cases/
          # content-based discovery would otherwise index this repo's own docs and eval fixtures; only eval-sandbox/** is a requirement source here
          requirements_paths: |
            !docs/**
            !eval/**
            !research/**
            !README.md
            !skills/**
            !.github/**
            !ccr/**
          # TEMPORARY test credential and model (the Copilot quota is used up): remove `|| secrets.SPEC` and the model pin when done (model back to `${{ vars.SPECGUARD_EVAL_MODEL }}`)
          llm_token: ${{ secrets.SPECGUARD_LLM_TOKEN || secrets.SPEC }}
          model: haiku-5.5
          max_comments: "${{ vars.SPECGUARD_EVAL_MAX_COMMENTS || '10' }}"
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
        with: { name: specguard-ctx, path: .specguard-ctx/, retention-days: 7, include-hidden-files: true }
